findings.why_it_is_not_F1: the line is a fixture docstring, ordinary English about a transport adapter's parse_body, the same class as the reddit_feed.py:65 line the driver counted; it names no library item (the library's craft belonged to a pack, never to an adapter); it predates the run (7fb3c8c8, 2026-09-02). The ticket's Details say a fourth survivor is a finding; I deviate on its class -- it is a finding about the count in the record, not about a shipped file naming a retired item -- and report the deviation here with the grep output as its evidence.

state_facts_not_findings: A ring item that is neither a root (no adapter:) nor a narrowing (no narrows:) resolves at pin time as a bare link: the chain walk in standards_support._chain returns when declared_narrows is empty and resolve_chain only counts adapters. The re-applied deleted test shows exactly this at the tip (the callable opened). tools/validate.py refuses such an item in the library tree ('missing required key narrows'), but pin_fields does not validate a ring item's frontmatter. This predates the repair -- the only pin-time guard was the legacy standards: door, which never fired for an item carrying no such key -- and no unit of this run owned it. Recorded as successor scope: a pin-time refusal of a manifest that declares neither adapter: nor narrows:, or a validator pass over ring items at resolution.
The repair's report and the driver's Details both anticipated two derived files moving under regen; one moved. Not a finding: regen --check is current and the report says so.
The first round's F4, F5, F7, F8, F9, F10 remain exactly as recorded; nothing this round touched their sites.

The whole test_ticket_pins module under the mutant lost two tests, not one: the chain-level test_a_resolved_set_carrying_two_adapters_refuses is a second, independent check on the same door. The rule the deleted test asserted is therefore held at two seams.
